description: Two mobile header architectures coexist. Standard routes render a two-row topbar (context+actions row, then a full-width search row); focus-canvas routes (chat/code/analyze/explore) render a single compact row with search hidden. The same product announces itself with two different header grammars.
measured_value: topbar height: 107px (standard) vs 65px (focus-canvas) at 390px; search row display flex vs none
expected_rule: R-NAV-1: one header architecture for all /app routes; single row <=64px below 768px; search lives in the row, not a second row
recommendation: Unify on the single-row compact header; move global search into the actions cluster (icon trigger) at <768px; adopt the focus-canvas header as the reference and delete the two-row variant.

description: Fixed chrome consumes ~21% of the viewport at 390px (two-row topbar 107px + bottom bar 70px = 177px of 844px). No vertical budget was ever declared for mobile chrome, so navigation outbids content.
measured_value: chromeRatio = 21% at 390 / 19% at 430; contentVisible = 667px of 844px
expected_rule: R-NAV-2: mobile chrome budget <=15% of viewport height at 390px (<=128px: 56px header + 64px tab bar + 8px offsets)
recommendation: Declare the 390px vertical budget as a system contract (NAVIGATION-ARCHITECTURE.md table); compress header to one row; slim tab bar to 64px incl. safe-area handling.

description: Page identity is announced twice: the topbar context label shows the active destination AND the page body renders its own h1 (e.g. 'الإعدادات' in both the header and the page). The duplicated title costs vertical space and dilutes hierarchy.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements chrome.contextRow.title vs geom.titles.h1 per route; screenshots/settings/390-viewport.jpg
measured_value: topbar title text === page h1 text on all routes (e.g. 'الإعدادات' / 'الإعدادات')
expected_rule: R-NAV-3: exactly one source of page identity per route; the header shows workspace context, the page owns the title
recommendation: Keep the topbar label as the persistent context cue but treat the page h1 as the single title block; never render both at the same visual weight; consider removing the header label once a route h1 is visible.

description: Two bottom-navigation dialects: full-width glass bar (standard routes) vs floating rounded dock with glow indicator (focus-canvas routes). Different edge treatment, radius, shadow, and active indicator language.
measured_value: bottom nav: 70px full-width inset 0 (standard) vs 66px floating inset-inline 16px radius 16px (focus)
expected_rule: R-NAV-4: one dock grammar at <768px: floating dock, 16px inset, 64px height, one active-indicator treatment
recommendation: Adopt the floating dock as the single mobile nav; drop the full-width bar; keep safe-area reserve token.

description: Drawer information architecture is not encoded in visual weight: 19 destinations in 4 groups, but every link renders at identical size/height (15.36px / 44px). Group labels exist, yet 'الخدمات' items, advanced tools, and operations carry the same weight; the utility group ('مكتبتي / الإعدادات') is unlabelled.
measured_value: all 19 links: fontSize 15.36px, height 44px; group label font 10.5px; nav scrolls internally (scrollable=true)
expected_rule: R-NAV-5: three-tier weight system in the drawer: core services (primary weight), workspace/advanced (secondary), operations/administration (tertiary); utility group labelled 'مساحتي'
recommendation: Introduce tiered link weights (size/leading/color steps via tokens), label the utility group, and give the primary tier a distinct register (see NAVIGATION-ARCHITECTURE.md drawer spec).

description: Search exists in three uncoordinated forms: the topbar global trigger (opens ⌘K palette), per-page library toolbars (local filtering), and workspace quick-search affordances. The scopes are not visually distinguished, so search reads as a repeated decorative element rather than a scoped function.
measured_value: 3 search surfaces detected in code; toolbar search label 'ابحث في هذه المكتبة' vs global 'ابحث في منسج…'
expected_rule: R-NAV-6: search is scoped - global command palette (⌘K, icon in header) vs contextual in-page filter (inside the section it filters); a page carries an in-page search field only when it owns a filterable collection
recommendation: Differentiate the affordances: global = icon+kbd trigger; contextual = field inside the collection toolbar; document the scope rule; remove search fields from pages that do not filter a collection.

description: Translucent glass chrome (78% white + 20px blur) intentionally lets scrolled content show beneath the sticky header. The owner perceives 'text behind/under the header'. Not a clipping defect (anchor scroll-margin is correct); it is a transparency-level design decision awaiting an owner call.
measured_value: topbar background alpha 0.78 (light) / 0.66 (dark); scroll-margin-block-start = topbar+20px on anchors
expected_rule: R-NAV-7: chrome surfaces at >=0.92 opacity OR solid, with blur retained for the dock only
recommendation: Present owner with A/B (0.78 glass vs 0.95 near-solid); default recommendation: raise topbar to 0.95 and keep the floating dock glassy (the dock reads as an object, the header as structure).

description: Page h1 sizes come from at least four per-family conventions, not one scale: home 37.05px, library 34px, chat 33.15px, ops pages 28px (x9 routes), domain workspaces 23px (x6 routes). The first thing a user reads changes weight from screen to screen.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements aggregate.json -> geom.titles.h1 per route at 390
measured_value: h1 @390: 37.05 / 34 / 33.15 / 28 / 23 px (5 distinct values across 19 routes)
expected_rule: R-TYPE-1: one heading ramp; page h1 = 26px at 390 scaling to 34px at 1440 (token --mj-text-h1), no per-family overrides
recommendation: Map every route h1 onto the unified type ramp (DESIGN-TOKENS.md); delete per-family hero clamps from home/chat/library CSS.

description: The settings screen renders as a different product: sharp-cornered sections (12px radius only, 4 of 5 cards with no shadow) versus the app standard (16px radius, shadowed cards); section padding 19px and gaps 11-13px are off the token scale; a dashed upload box adds a utility aesthetic absent elsewhere.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements settings/390.json (radiusHistogram {12px:5}, shadowUsage {none:4,shadow:1}); globals.css:1523 .settings-section {padding:19px; border; background} (no radius); VLM perceptual settings390.json
measured_value: settings: 1 radius value (12px), 80% shadowless cards; home: 16px radius dominant, 80% shadowed
expected_rule: R-SURF-1..3: settings rebuilt on mj-surface primitives (16px base radius, xs shadow, --mj-pad-card padding)
recommendation: Rebuild settings sections on mj-surface + mj-section; retire the settings-* parallel classes (see COMPONENT-INVENTORY.md migration table).

route: knowledge, projects, agents, flows, runs, team
description: Homogeneous record collections render as stacks of equal cards; every record is a boxed container with header/body/footer, so lists compete with summary cards and the page reads as 'a stack of disconnected boxes' (perceptual pass).
evidence_reference: VLM perceptual knowledge390full.json; evidence/measurements knowledge/390.json (9 card-like containers)
measured_value: 9 card-like containers on one list page; identical card structure repeated per record
expected_rule: R-PAT-1: list pattern for homogeneous records (divided rows, one container), cards reserved for summaries/summaries-of-one
recommendation: Introduce the mj-data-list row pattern (already exists in layout.css) as the default for ops record lists; keep cards for stats/summaries only.

description: Spacing is authored as raw values, not tokens: 91 distinct padding values in the 14 universal layers plus 95 more in globals.css (186 total), against an 8-step gap scale and 2 padding tokens that already exist. This is the root cause of rhythm drift the owner perceives.
evidence_reference: scripts/css-analysis (distinct_padding_values: 91 universal + 95 globals); top raw paddings 12px/10px/14px/9px/11px
measured_value: 186 distinct padding values vs 10 spacing tokens defined
expected_rule: R-SPACE-1: all padding/margin/gap values resolve to the --mj-space scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48); raw px spacing forbidden outside tokens
recommendation: Adopt the consolidated space scale (DESIGN-TOKENS.md); migrate dialect paddings onto it; add a lint guard (IMP-02).
status: in-progress-phase-1 (begins per master doc 6: space scale adopted, legacy --mj-gap-* rebound to the 9-step scale, 398 exact-map declarations tokenized; raw padding distinct 155 -> 141, raw spacing distinct 243 -> 210; completion rides Phases 2-5 as surfaces are rebuilt)

description: Inter-section rhythm varies ~3x across route families at 390px: domain workspaces median 14px, home 22px, ops pages 30.1px, usage/billing 41.1px. The same app breathes at three different tempos.
measured_value: section-gap medians: 14px (learn/research/create/code/analyze/explore) / 22px (home) / 30.1px (ops) / 41.1px (usage/billing)
expected_rule: R-SPACE-2: one section rhythm token --mj-gap-block (24px at 390 -> 48px at 1440) between page sections on every route
recommendation: Bind each family's section spacing to the shared token; delete per-family block gaps.

description: Intra-page rhythm is unstable: zero-gap adjacencies (gapMin=0 on every route) coexist with gaps up to 68px in the same page column.
measured_value: gapMin=0 on all 19 routes; gapMax up to 68px (models) within a single page
expected_rule: R-SPACE-3: adjacent sections never touch; minimum inter-section gap = --mj-space-200 (24px at 390)
recommendation: Audit zero-gap adjacencies per route; enforce the floor in the page template (PAGE-PATTERNS-AND-MOTION.md).

description: Two parallel type ramps coexist (--u-text-xs..xl in foundations vs --mj-text-hero..caption in layout) plus per-page clamps; at 390px the app renders 22 distinct computed font sizes; the CSS declares 23 distinct font-size values.
evidence_reference: foundations.css:177-181 vs layout.css:41-54; css-analysis (23 declared sizes); aggregate fontSizeHistogram (22 computed sizes @390)
measured_value: 2 ramps + 22 live sizes at one viewport; dominant sizes 12px(x511), 15.36px(x227), 13.44px(x218)
expected_rule: R-TYPE-1: a single 11-level ramp (display..code) with one naming namespace; line-heights and Arabic rules bound to each level
recommendation: Consolidate to one ramp (DESIGN-TOKENS.md type table); alias --u-text-* to the ramp during migration; delete per-page clamps.

route: flows editor, run detail, learn checks, preview surfaces
description: Sub-9px text renders in product surfaces: 7px (.flow-node__footer, .preview-activity li>span) and 8px (.run-timeline__rail span, .test-citations span, .flow-start-label, .preview-inspector__head). Below any readable threshold on mobile.
measured_value: font sizes 7px and 8px in mono labels | after Phase 1 (2026-09-22): 0 sub-10px declarations (evidence/baselines/phase1/g7-baseline.json)
expected_rule: R-TYPE-2: minimum text size 10px (mono technical labels 10px minimum, prefer 11px); nothing smaller ships
recommendation: Raise the 7/8px labels to 10-11px; add a min-font-size lint rule.
status: resolved-in-phase-1 (Gate A: build/eslint/stylelint clean, hOverflow 0 x100, tapUnder44 unchanged; Gate B-3: sub-10px declarations 23 -> 0 measured by G-7 phase1 baseline; mono labels raised to --mj-text-code 12.5px or R-TYPE-2 floor 10/11px in fixed badges)

description: Arabic letter-spacing violations: .eyebrow / .page-eyebrow / .section-heading__eyebrow apply 0.08em tracking + uppercase to Arabic text; .mj-data-list__head and .mj-section__label apply 0.02em; .preview-hero h1 keeps -0.018em tracking in Arabic. Tracking tears Arabic's connected script; the zero-tracking law exists in design-system.md but is not enforced.
measured_value: tracking 0.08em/0.02em/-0.018em on Arabic-rendering classes without [lang=ar]/[dir=rtl] zero overrides | after Phase 1 (2026-09-22): 0 unpaired letter-spacing declarations (evidence/baselines/phase1/g7-baseline.json)
expected_rule: R-RTL-1: letter-spacing: 0 on all Arabic text; tracking allowed only on Latin strings (html[lang=en] scope or .ltr-value)
recommendation: Add [lang=ar] zero-tracking overrides for every tracking class; add lint rule scanning letter-spacing without an Arabic override.
status: resolved-in-phase-1 (Gate A clean; Gate B-3: 37 tracking candidates -> 6 legal (2 [lang=en]-scoped ramp rules, 2 latin-only marketing rules, 2 rtl-paired) with 0 UNPAIRED measured by the upgraded G-7 per-selector pairing check; 30 unpaired trackings deleted)

description: The reading stack is small-size-heavy: the most frequent text size at 390px is 12px (511 instances), ahead of body 15.36px and 13.44px. Labels/captions dominate the visual field, contributing to the 'everything looks like different shades of the same thing' perception.
measured_value: 12px x511 vs 15.36px x227 vs 13.44px x218 instances
expected_rule: R-TYPE-3: body text = 15-16px; secondary 13-14px; captions/labels 12px reserved for metadata, not primary content
recommendation: Rebalance content strings to body sizes per the type ramp usage rules; audit routes where 12px carries content.

description: Two brand color systems: marketing Tailwind @theme palette (brand-cyan #06b6d4, brand-emerald #047857, brand-pink #ec4899...) vs app tokens (--u-cyan #0b8cab, --u-mint #0d9f70, --u-pink #e2579a). Same hue families, different values; brand continuity breaks at the marketing/product boundary.
evidence_reference: foundations.css:33-58 (@theme) vs :root block; css-analysis (364 hardcoded hex in layers)
measured_value: marketing cyan #06b6d4 vs app cyan #0b8cab; emerald #047857 vs mint #0d9f70; pink #ec4899 vs #e2579a
expected_rule: R-COL-1: one brand palette; marketing utilities consume the same underlying values (theme bridge), never independent hex
recommendation: Bridge @theme colors to var(--u-*) equivalents (or redefine both from one source); document the bridge in DESIGN-TOKENS.md.

description: 22+ accent-family colors are active (7 service jewel tones + 5 status tones + 3 brand steps + 7 marketing hues + 4 cover-art hues). Accent roles are not bound to screen positions, so cyan/green/purple/amber appear in different roles on different screens - each screen can read as having its own theme.
evidence_reference: foundations.css service blocks (371-388), status tints (108-120), cover art (122-131), marketing theme (37-50)
measured_value: 7 service colors + 5 status + 3 brand + 7 marketing + 4 cover = 26 accent-family values
expected_rule: R-COL-2: accent roles are semantic and positional - primary (indigo) for interaction only, service hue for identity thread only (<=10% area), status tones for status only; an accent color may never change meaning between screens
recommendation: Publish the semantic color role table (DESIGN-TOKENS.md) with allowed positions; audit usages against it; forbid ad-hoc accent assignment.

description: The focus-canvas system (--fc-* tokens: separate glass, line, raise, ink, accent sets) introduces a third surface language used by 4 of 19 routes. It is well-built but unaccounted for in the public token model, so the app has three surface stories (standard light/dark, focus canvas, marketing dark).
measured_value: --fc-* defines 15 parallel tokens overriding shell chrome on 4 routes
expected_rule: R-SURF-4: at most two declared canvases app-wide (standard, focus); each is a named, documented token set - no undeclared third surface language
recommendation: Either fold --fc-* into the standard surface scale or formally declare the focus canvas as the second canvas in DESIGN-TOKENS.md with its own contract.

route: learn, research, create, code, analyze, explore, home
description: Surface inflation, measured: on domain workspaces nearly every card is nested inside another card - learn 14/15, research 13/14, create 10/11, code 11/12, analyze 8/9, explore 8/9; home nests 8/20 including depth-3 (card-in-card-in-card). The anti-nesting law exists in layout.css but dialect classes bypass mj-surface.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements aggregate.json -> nestingDepthHistogram @390; layout.css:346-362 (anti-nesting law); VLM perceptual (home390scrolled: 'input nested in larger container that serves no clear purpose')
measured_value: nested card ratios at 390: learn 93%, research 93%, create 91%, code 92%, analyze 89%, explore 89%, home 40% (max depth 3)
expected_rule: R-SURF-1: a surface never contains another surface of equal or higher level; grouping inside a surface = stack + spacing, or a --flat inline group
recommendation: Refactor the u2-workbench and service-space interiors onto mj-surface--flat groups; cap the tree at surface > flat-group > controls.

description: Radius is not tied to hierarchy: five radius values are live at 390px (12px x89, 16px x72, pill x23, 22px x14, 24px x2) and the CSS declares 23 distinct radius values. Controls, cards, overlays and navigation pick radii per component.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements aggregate.json -> radiusHistogram @390; css-analysis (23 declared values incl. asymmetric 7px 7px 2px 7px)
measured_value: 5 live radius values at 390; 23 declared globally; asymmetric quirks present
expected_rule: R-SURF-2: radius maps to surface level - 8px controls / 12px inputs / 16px cards / 22px overlays / pill for chips; nothing else
recommendation: Bind radii to the level map (DESIGN-TOKENS.md); replace the asymmetric quirks; lint guard.

description: Elevation is unregulated: 71 distinct box-shadow values across the layers versus the 5-step --u-shadow scale. Shadows are composed ad hoc per component, producing uneven depth.
measured_value: 71 distinct shadow declarations vs 5-step elevation scale
expected_rule: R-SURF-3: shadows only via --u-shadow-xs..xl tokens; one elevation step per surface level
recommendation: Replace raw shadows with elevation tokens; delete composite one-off shadows.

description: Container-measure fragmentation: 11 content widths are active (480/560/640/720/840/880/900/1040/1080/1240/1520) across 6 container-query ladders, while the IA documents a 5-step ladder. Reading measure and grid widths differ per family.
evidence_reference: responsive.css canonical ladders; IA section 5; ops-page max-width 1240; --mj-content-max 1520; universal-container 1240
measured_value: 11 distinct container widths in active use
expected_rule: R-GRD-1: 4-step measure ladder - narrow 560 / prose 780 / wide 1040 / full 1440; every page section declares one
recommendation: Collapse the ladder to four measures; map each existing width to the nearest step; document in RESPONSIVE-ARCHITECTURE.md.

description: Requesting the desktop site on a phone renders the tablet rail composition at unreadable physical sizes: at 980 CSS px the shell enters rail mode (76px icon sidebar); a nav link at 15.36px CSS becomes ~6.5px effective on a 414px-wide phone (scale 0.422). Desktop mode must not mean 'shrunken desktop UI'.
measured_value: effective nav text 6.5px; effective h1 24.5px; body text ~6px effective at phone scale
expected_rule: R-RES-1: wide-viewport + coarse pointer (pointer: coarse) serves the touch composition (drawer + tab bar + >=14px effective text); the rail/sidebar composition requires a fine pointer or >=1024px viewport
recommendation: Add a pointer-media guard to the viewport-mode hook: (pointer: coarse) forces the mobile shell regardless of width; document in RESPONSIVE-ARCHITECTURE.md.

description: Tablet (768-1023) defaults to a 76px icon rail with all labels hidden; expanding overlays content instead of pushing it. Icon-only rail on a touch-first tablet reduces discoverability of 19 destinations and differs from the desktop push behavior.
evidence_reference: shell.css tablet section; app-shell.tsx sidebar state machine
measured_value: rail 76px labels hidden at 768-1023; overlay mode vs desktop push mode
expected_rule: R-RES-2: tablet composition = expanded labeled sidebar by default at >=768 (push, not overlay) OR documented owner decision for rail; one behavior across the band
recommendation: Owner decision: labeled tablet sidebar (recommended) vs rail; then normalize overlay/push behavior accordingly.

description: Configuration precedes action on the shared gateway: 9 sections (contextual nav, welcome, toolbelt, mode cards, composer, four-step path, trust note, starters, mini-library) render before the first execution; 18 card-like surfaces compete. The guided/quick switch adds progressive disclosure, but the initial view still stacks every concern.
evidence_reference: docs/02-experience/page-specs.md C-0 (9 sections); evidence/measurements chat/390.json (18 card-like); VLM perceptual chat390 ('too airy between headline and input list... card-in-card active state')
measured_value: 9 pre-execution sections; 18 card-like containers at 390
expected_rule: R-PAT-2: creation flows are composer-first - prompt + primary action above the fold; configuration reveals progressively (mode, tools, advanced)
recommendation: Reorder the gateway: composer + primary CTA first; collapse toolbelt/path/trust/starters behind progressive disclosure; see PAGE-PATTERNS-AND-MOTION.md creation-flow template.

description: Route transitions run at 480ms ('expressive' token) with a 10px enter offset on every navigation - slow for wayfinding; platform norms sit at 200-300ms for route changes.
measured_value: route transition 480ms ease-enter on all navigations
expected_rule: R-MOT-1: route transitions 240ms; expressive (480ms) reserved for milestone moments, not wayfinding
recommendation: Retokenize route-in to 240ms; keep expressive for first-visit hero reveals only.

description: Two alert-red systems: the notification dot uses --u-shell-alert (pink #e75f9d) on standard chrome but #EF4444 on focus-canvas chrome.
measured_value: alert dot #e75f9d vs #EF4444
expected_rule: R-COL-3: one attention token --u-alert used by every chrome variant
recommendation: Bind both to a single alert token.

description: Accessibility engineering gates hold: every measured tap target >=44px (0 under 32px across routes), zero horizontal overflow at all five viewports, skip-link present, aria-current on active nav, focus-visible defined. This audit adds gates on top, it does not contradict this pass.
evidence_reference: evidence/measurements aggregate.json -> tapTargets per route; hOverflow=false x100 captures
measured_value: min target 44px; overflow 0/100 captures
expected_rule: keep as invariant gate (VISUAL-QA-CHECKLIST.md section A)
recommendation: Maintain; extend QA with reflow, target-size and heading-order checks at all five viewports.

description: Focus treatment is inconsistent: global :focus-visible outline 2.5px vs app-shell override 3px glow; kbd hint at 11px mono sits below the caption floor.
measured_value: outline-width 2.5px vs 3px; kbd 11px
expected_rule: R-ACC-1: one focus token (3px ring, offset 3px, both themes) and kbd >=11px mono with 10px floor
recommendation: Unify focus tokens; raise kbd to token size.

description: Seven coexisting component dialects: universal-shell-* (chrome), mj-* primitives (v20), u2-* workbench (262 classes / 616 selectors), service-* gateway, adaptive-* home, ops/settings/library classes in globals.css (480 classes / 1220 selectors), ms-* + Tailwind marketing. The v20 primitives cover a fraction of the rendered UI; the rest predates or bypasses them. This is the mechanical root of the 'assembled UI kit' perception.
evidence_reference: scripts/css-analysis per-layer census; workbench.css 616 selectors; globals.css 1220 selectors
measured_value: 7 dialects; 568 unique classes in universal layers + 480 in globals; workbench alone = 262 classes
expected_rule: R-IMP-1: one primitive layer (mj-*) consumed by all surfaces; dialect classes are migration targets, not additions
recommendation: Execute the consolidation plan in COMPONENT-INVENTORY.md (migration table per dialect).

description: No automated enforcement: the token laws (anti-nesting, spacing scale, radius map, Arabic zero-tracking, min font size) exist as CSS comments and prose only. Deviations accumulate silently between reviews.
evidence_reference: eslint.config.mjs (no style rules); absence of stylelint; laws in layout.css comments + design-system.md
measured_value: 0 lint rules guarding visual tokens
expected_rule: R-IMP-2: lint/build gates for token usage - raw spacing, raw radius, raw shadows, tracking without Arabic override, sub-10px text, nested surfaces
recommendation: Add stylelint + custom checks (see VISUAL-QA-CHECKLIST.md gate G-7); wire into the pre-push gate.

description: globals.css is an unlayered parallel system: 1985 lines / 1220 selectors outside the 14-layer architecture, carrying its own button system, page anatomy, and admin surfaces - including the divergent settings skin.
measured_value: 1985 lines; 1220 selectors; 480 classes; own .button--* system
expected_rule: R-IMP-3: every selector lives in a declared layer; globals.css contains only resets/edge cases after migration
recommendation: Port globals.css content into the layer files (shell/layout/states/ops) with token-compliant values; track in COMPONENT-INVENTORY.md.

description: Owner report: 'large empty/gray area inside the statistics card' on the knowledge screen. Current DOM shows the stats block filled (dl.ops-stats h=196px at 430, 4 stats in a 2x2 grid; a dead-space scan of every main element >120px tall with <40 chars found zero candidates). The empty area may belong to a transient state, another viewport/theme, or a since-changed build. Kept open per audit protocol - never deleted, never promoted.
measured_value: ops-stats: height 196px, 4 children, no dead-space candidates detected in current state
expected_rule: R-PAT-3: every reserved area is either a declared skeleton, a declared empty state with guidance, or removed; no unexplained voids
recommendation: Owner to confirm reproduction context (viewport/theme/state); if it was a loading state, bind skeletons to the stats card (states.css already provides them).

description: Owner report: 'page content/text appears behind or under the header during scrolling and route transitions'. Measured: content does scroll beneath the translucent header by design (glass 0.78 + blur); anchor scroll-margins are correct; the route-enter animation starts 10px below rest. No hard clipping reproduced in 100 captures. Perception may be the transparency + enter-offset combination.
measured_value: no clipping found; glass alpha 0.78; enter offset 10px/480ms
expected_rule: R-NAV-7 (same as NAV-07)
recommendation: Bundle with the NAV-07 owner decision; if confirmed as disturbing, raise chrome opacity to 0.95 and reduce enter offset to 4px/240ms.

description: Owner report: 'content approaches or appears cut behind the bottom navigation'. Measured: content bottom padding includes the tab-bar reserve (--mj-tabbar-reserve = 80px + safe-area; 112px on focus routes) on every route; no element renders beneath the bar in captures. Perception may come from the bar's shadow/glass weight.
measured_value: reserve honored on all routes; 0 overlap findings
expected_rule: R-NAV-4 weight sub-rule: the dock's visual weight (shadow+glass+pill) is capped
recommendation: Owner decision on dock weight; options in NAVIGATION-ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.
